inputPapers.title: STP-GUI: Spatially-Aware Token Pruning for Efficient Web-GUI Agents
inputPapers.abstract: With the rapid development of vision-language models (VLMs), Web-GUI agents have achieved promising performance in interacting with real-world interfaces through screenshot-based grounding. However, high-resolution screenshots and multi-turn histories introduce excessive visual tokens, causing substantial inference overhead. Existing token pruning methods, mainly designed for natural images, often select tokens independently based on importance scores, which can fragment the local visual structures required for recognizing small GUI elements such as buttons, icons, and hyperlinks. In this work, we propose STP-GUI (Spatially-aware Token Pruning for GUI agents), a query-guided token pruning framework that preserves fine-grained instruction-conditioned token scoring while performing spatially coherent window-level selection under aggressive token reduction. A lightweight selector is optimized through policy learning while the VLM backbone remains frozen. Experiments on Online-Mind2Web show that \papername achieves a favorable efficiency-performance tradeoff under low token budgets. At 21% token retention, it preserves 77.7% of full-token performance while reducing inference latency by 31% and FLOPs by 57%. Results on Android in the Wild further suggest that the method transfers to mobile GUI environments.

inputPapers.title: Look Before You Restore: Learning to Predict Before Acting for Agentic Image Restoration
inputPapers.abstract: Agents for mixed-degradation image restoration typically learn what a tool does to an image only after running it: failed calls waste computation and harmful outputs go unnoticed until too late. We propose PreActIR, an agentic restoration framework that predicts tool consequences before execution. For each candidate tool, a tool-conditioned world model forecasts changes in residual degradation, image quality, and fidelity, together with the risk of harm and the uncertainty of the prediction. The agent executes the top-ranked candidate, and an independent verifier commits or rolls back its output before the agent replans from the observed state. PreActIR also audits whether performance is limited by the selector or by the candidate space, and studies targeted tool adaptation as a controlled way to expand that space. In a controlled evaluation that fixes the candidate pool, verifier, and budget and employs reference-annotated degradation states, PreActIR uses 42.5% fewer real tool calls and 63.4% fewer rejected calls than reactive, execute-then-evaluate trial and error, while improving Y-PSNR by 0.92 dB.

inputPapers.title: ReferFlow: Beyond Final-Target Localization for Complex Referring Expressions
inputPapers.abstract: Multimodal Large Language Models have made significant progress in referring expression comprehension (REC), yet most REC benchmarks still focus on final-target localization. Complex queries often involve intermediate visual references with different dependencies on prior grounding, but final-only evaluation leaves this process unexamined. To address this gap, we formulate trajectory-level REC, in which models receive an ordered sequence of grounding steps constructed from a single complex query and localize the target regions associated with each step. We instantiate this setting in ReferFlow-Bench, which characterizes structured region transitions through four trajectory types, namely Refinement, Shift, Reset, and Mixture. Experiments show that current models struggle to consistently ground intermediate visual references across successive steps. We further propose ReferFlow, which decouples interleaved text-latent trajectory generation from coordinate decoding. Specifically, Stateful Region Latent Reasoning represents each target region as an object-indexed state composed of continuous latents, with explicit visual and spatial supervision to preserve region information for subsequent grounding. Trajectory-Aware Parallel Decoding then recovers all coordinate blocks in parallel through four geometry-constrained refinement rounds, with each block conditioned on its corresponding trajectory prefix, thereby reducing within-box sequential dependencies and eliminating cross-box autoregression. We further apply Grounding-Aware GRPO to promote consistent grounding across steps and learn adaptive trajectory generation from complex REC queries. ReferFlow achieves leading performance on general REC benchmarks and ReferFlow-Bench.

inputPapers.title: InfiniSplat v2: Analyzing and Improving Feed-Forward 3DGS from Any Views
inputPapers.abstract: Feed-forward Gaussian reconstruction builds 3D scenes directly from input images for novel view rendering, but learning Gaussian attributes from predicted geometry for high-quality rendering under large viewpoint changes remains challenging. We analyze limitations in Gaussian attribute learning and introduce InfiniSplat v2, which improves rendering quality through architectural and training changes. Our method decouples geometry and attribute prediction with a frozen geometry branch, aligns predicted Gaussians using ground-truth camera poses during training, and adopts large-angle target view supervision. Across six datasets, the feed-forward outputs of the same trained model achieve state-of-the-art mean LPIPS and DISTS among the evaluated methods in both pose-conditioned and pose-free settings. In the pose-conditioned setting, mean LPIPS and DISTS decrease by 25.8% and 32.9%, respectively, compared with the strongest evaluated baselines. We further find that opacity learned with only image reconstruction supervision suppresses geometrically inconsistent points. Project page: https://zju3dv.github.io/InfiniSplat2/

inputPapers.title: Read, Parse, Describe: Unified Document Parsing with Visual Element Description Generation
inputPapers.abstract: Document understanding systems are typically evaluated as separate components via layout analysis, optical text recognition, reading-order prediction, and image captioning. This separation leaves scientific figures, captions, and visual semantics weakly connected, and fails to measure whether a model can produce a single page-level parse that is both structurally faithful and semantically accessible. We introduce Read-Parse-Describe, a unified dataset for document parsing with visual element description generation. Given a page image, models are required to output an ordered list of layout elements containing bounding boxes, semantic labels, reading-order indices, recognized textual content, and alternative text descriptions for visual elements. The benchmark is built from 2,402 documents, comprising 18,163 continuous pages, 125,218 layout elements, and 11,338 visual instances. Besides, we further propose a plug-and-play space-awareness enhancer that reuses multi-layer visual features and injects grid-aware spatial guidance into vision-language tokens for layout-aware generation. Experiments across end-to-end VLMs and pipeline parsers show that existing systems still struggle to jointly recover reading order and visual semantics, while our enhanced model achieves strong joint performance. These results highlight the need to move beyond isolated document parsing modules toward unified models that jointly read, parse, and describe complex documents. The new dataset and code will be made publicly available at https://github.com/yufanchen96/RPD

inputPapers.title: Beyond Static Cues: Unified Dynamic Detection of MLLM Backdoors via Dual-Flow Trajectory Analysis
inputPapers.abstract: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) are increasingly deployed in safety-critical domains, yet their susceptibility to backdoor attacks remains a formidable challenge. While existing defenses have evolved from visual-centric patch cues to unsupervised internal attention statistics, they are fundamentally constrained by a reliance on static snapshots and attack-specific heuristics. Given the intricate interplay between dual modalities, the vast design space for multimodal triggers allows diverse threats, such as textual injections, sub-perceptual noises, and coordinated cross-modal triggers, to easily circumvent such rigid priors, particularly when attack types are unknown in real-world applications. In this paper, we rethink backdoor detection by shifting the diagnostic paradigm from static observations to dynamic output evolution. We observe that a successful attack inevitably hijacks the model's decoding trajectory, skewing internal modal contributions during generation while maintaining an abnormal output invariance despite input perturbations. To capture this behavior, we propose EVO-Detect, a unified detection framework that monitors the dynamic evolution of internal signals during early decoding steps through two complementary channels: Attention Flow and Logits Flow. The attention branch measures how image-text attention allocation evolves during early generation, whereas the logits branch quantifies the sensitivity of the output distribution to modal perturbations through interventional ablations. We then convert these trajectories into compact sample-level metrics and normalize them against negative-control signatures so that natural perturbations are less likely to be mistaken for backdoor evidence. Extensive evaluations show that our approach substantially outperforms state-of-the-art baselines such as BYE and TCAP across diverse attack families.

inputPapers.title: Event Cameras versus Frame Cameras for Synthetic-Aperture Imaging: A Simulation Study
inputPapers.abstract: Synthetic-aperture imaging (SAI) removes occluders such as foliage by integrating many views of a scene along a camera path. It has so far been used mainly with frame cameras. We ask whether an event camera has advantages for SAI, and answer the question in simulation, where both sensors see exactly the same scene and the same camera movement. A densely rendered Blender sequence is turned into frames with an EMVA~1288 noise model of an industrial global-shutter camera, and into an event stream with the v2e simulator parameterized like a Sony IMX636. The frames are integrated with the existing airborne optical sectioning renderer. For the events we add a new integration path that projects every single event onto the focal plane at its own interpolated pose, so no events have to be binned into frames. We compare the two sensors in three main runs and an additional dark high-speed test. In a bright scene at 25,m/s the frame camera records only three images on the path and cannot remove the occluder, while the event camera reconstructs the target, even after an event-rate controller drops most of its events to fit the camera link. At the same speed in a 5,lux scene the event camera no longer resolves the target either. In a 5,lux scene at 5,m/s both sensors reconstruct the target at similar quality. We also compare the data one traversal of the aperture costs. At high speed the capped event stream still shows the target at the same data volume as the three frames. At 1,m/s we compare both cameras at two matched data budgets, and there the event camera has no advantage over the frame camera in reconstruction quality. The data rate of the event camera depends on the scene and is highest exactly in the fast bright scenes where it is needed most.

inputPapers.title: A Valid Watermark Is Not a Valid Identity: Spatial-Spectral Adversarial Face Evasion with Watermark Preservation
inputPapers.abstract: Facial image watermarking can support traceability and certification in biometric pipelines, but provenance or manipulation detection alone does not guarantee reliable biometric identity. We introduce a watermark-preserving face evasion attack that targets this gap under a black-box watermarking setting, without access to the watermarking components. The proposed PGD-L_2 attack guides adversarial perturbations with spatial and spectral preservation terms to reduce face-recognition similarity while limiting pixel-level distortion and high-frequency changes that may interfere with hidden watermark cues. Evaluated on controlled facial images with two watermarking schemes, two face-recognition models, and two datasets, the attack achieves evasion rates above 92% at operational thresholds while preserving watermark recovery above 93% for StegaFormer and above 99.7% for FaceSigns, with visual quality above 47dB PSNR at epsilon_2=2.0. These results expose a structural gap in watermark-based facial certification: a face image can remain watermark-valid and visually faithful while becoming biometrically unreliable.

inputPapers.title: Resolution Allocation with Learnable Resizing and Spectral Filter Parameterization
inputPapers.abstract: Learnable downsampling and spectral-domain filter parameterizations have each made convolutional networks more flexible, but their interaction has not been systematically examined. We bridge this gap by examining convolutional kernels learned in the spatial and spectral domains, together with learned downsampling ratios under a cropped resizing implementation. We find that spectral and spatial kernels respond differently to learned resolution allocation, with larger gains for the spectral kernel. We observe this consistently on three datasets (EuroSAT, CIFAR-10 and STL-10) and at two model sizes (differences in accuracy gain of +0.013 to +0.028 on held-out test sets). Part of this difference reflects the greater gain of the spectral kernel from retaining more spatial area, but the difference remains positive when total retained area is matched. This pattern is observed across datasets and model sizes, although its magnitude and dependence on the complexity budget vary with model size and the resizing implementation.

inputPapers.title: GLoD-LVSM: Learning Geometry-Grounded Continuous-LoD Scene Representations for Large View Synthesis Models
inputPapers.abstract: Large view synthesis models (LVSMs) reconstruct scenes from sparse views and render novel views quickly, but they incur unnecessary storage and rendering costs due to token redundancy. We present GLoD-LVSM, a compact, geometry-grounded scene representation for LVSMs with continuous levels of detail. First, instead of learning a fixed set of scene anchor initializations, GLoD-LVSM learns a continuous field that initializes a flexible number of anchors to match the desired budget. A condenser then aggregates scene information into these anchors, with both the field and condenser trained end-to-end. Second, the condenser infers reference-token and anchor geometry to guide compression through geometry-grounded attention, improving rendering quality and enabling frustum culling during decoding. Compared with existing LVSM scene-compression baselines, GLoD-LVSM achieves the best trade-off between rendering quality and scene token count. Compared with the uncompressed base model, GLoD-LVSM reduces the scene-token count by 33.4% and accelerates rendering by $1.23\times$ with no quality loss. Under a relaxed quality-loss budget, the reduction increases to 85.5%, with $3.00\times$ rendering speedup. Further analysis reveals that view-synthesis supervision yields emergent scene depth and self-organized anchors that align with surfaces and adapt their density to local texture complexity. Beyond rendering, we further show that our scene representation also supports scene-semantic understanding, highlighting its potential for broader downstream tasks.

inputPapers.title: Contrastive uncertainty learning for robust multi-structure segmentation in lower-pelvic MR
inputPapers.abstract: Boundary delineation of anatomical structures in prostate MRI is often compromised by regional ambiguity. Automated segmentation methods relying on global overlap loss functions tend to be insensitive to surface deviations, leading to significant errors in ambiguous regions. Most existing uncertainty-aware methods treat uncertainty as a post-hoc quality indicator or prediction filter. We propose Contrastive Uncertainty Learning (CUL), a supervised framework that uses predictive uncertainty to directly guide representation learning. Using Monte Carlo Dropout, CUL identifies voxel-wise uncertainty and structures the embedding geometry accordingly: low-uncertainty, correctly predicted features form stable voxels while high-uncertainty or misclassified features are actively repelled, preventing feature collapse at difficult boundaries. We evaluate CUL on a 589-scan 3D prostate MRI multi-structure segmentation task (8 anatomical structures) using a ViT with UperNet decoder architecture. Average Dice ($83.38\%$) remains comparable to the baseline ($83.35\%$), while surface distance decreases significantly ($p<0.001$) across 6 of 8 anatomical structures. A hard-case analysis reveals a $22{\times}$ asymmetry between significantly improved and degraded cases ($18.8\%$ vs $0.9\%$). Ablation studies show that removing uncertainty-guided sample selection eliminates improvements for the transition zone, while replacing the contrastive objective with a boundary loss additionally removes bladder improvements, demonstrating that both uncertainty-guided sampling and the contrastive objective are essential for the observed gains. These findings demonstrate that the proposed uncertainty-guided representation learning is a useful mechanism for reducing the risk of extreme errors in safety-critical medical segmentation

inputPapers.title: PAWA: Panoramic Action-conditioned World Modeling for Multiple Agents
inputPapers.abstract: A multiplayer world model must predict how the independent actions of several players change a shared environment, including changes outside a player's current field of view. A point-of-view (POV) video captures such changes only after they enter its field of view, whereas panoramic video records the surroundings in every viewing direction and has served as an intermediate representation of the world state in recent world models. Learning this task therefore requires synchronized POV and panoramic videos of interacting players together with their actions, yet no existing dataset provides this combination in Minecraft, an established testbed in which players act independently in a shared, modifiable 3D world. We present PAWA, a dataset and framework for action-conditioned panoramic multiplayer world modeling. The dataset pairs each player's POV video with world-stabilized panoramic video and aligned actions. Its distributed pipeline decouples CPU gameplay capture from GPU rendering, scales beyond 64 simultaneous players, and re-renders each recorded session under new observation configurations without replaying the gameplay. On this dataset, we develop a dual-tower model that jointly predicts POV and panoramic video and couples the two streams through cross-attention that aligns tokens observing the same direction in a shared world frame. We further introduce a quadratic-phase player encoding that provides many more player codes than existing rotary codes at the same embedding dimension. Experiments show that PAWA outperforms state-of-the-art multiplayer world models in POV prediction quality while also producing high-fidelity panoramic predictions. The dataset and collection pipeline are open source to support further research on multiplayer world models.

inputPapers.title: Glance Forcing: Making Bidirectional Diffusion Autoregressive at a Glance
inputPapers.abstract: Autoregressive generation underlies real-time, causal video synthesis and is the backbone of video world models. Today's dominant approach distills a bidirectional diffusion model into a causal few-step student, but existing pipelines make this conversion prohibitively expensive, requiring offline Probability Flow ODE} (PF-ODE) trajectories that cost tens of thousands of GPU-hours and terabytes of storage. We show it can be made dramatically more efficient. Pushing this efficiency to its extreme, we reduce trajectory supervision to a single sample, the strictest setting possible, and find that it causes severe quality collapse. We trace this to the teacher's trajectory geometry: the high-noise regime, governing semantic layout and motion, and the low-noise regime, governing fine texture exhibit fundamentally different curvature and optimization behavior, so a single monolithic student cannot jointly fit both, causing severe representation interference. Motivated by this, we propose Glance Forcing, a lightweight distillation framework that decouples the denoising trajectory into two complementary slow and fast experts, each guided by a tailored, stage-specific objective, while keeping the pretrained teacher entirely frozen. This decoupling further reveals a general mechanism underlying few-step distillation: PF-ODE distillation mainly straightens the few-step trajectory geometry, while the subsequent distribution-matching stage independently governs distributional quality. Using only one PF-ODE trajectory, Glance Forcing already surpasses the fully-trained state-of-the-art baseline, raising the VBench Total score from 84.04 to 84.22 while cutting trajectory-collection cost from thousands of GPU-hours to about one A100-GPU-hour, with markedly larger gains in dynamic degree, VisionReward, and instruction-following, and consistent preference from human raters over strong baselines.

inputPapers.title: Continual pretraining Prostate MRI ViT Encoder for task alignment
inputPapers.abstract: Building foundation models for MRI has emerged as a promising direction for advancing medical image analysis and improving accessibility of task specific models. Existing approaches primarily focus on effective pretraining strategies and evaluating their performance across diverse downstream tasks. While these methods show performance gains, limited attention has been given to understanding task alignment between pretraining and downstream objectives. Unlike language models, where the two stages are naturally aligned, such alignment is less evident in vision based applications. Motivated by this gap, we explore continual pretraining. Specifically, continually pretraining a pretrained ViT encoder using Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) on a prostate segmentation task to enhance task alignment and downstream performance. We further perform layer-wise representational analysis using Centered Kernel Alignment (CKA) to assess representational shifts and their correlation with task outcomes. Our experiments show improved performance in 3 of 6 downstream tasks and comparable results in the others. Our Feature analysis reveals that, for segmentation tasks, continually pretrained encoder features exhibit greater similarity to those of the finetuned encoder than the original pretrained encoder, correlating with observed performance gains.

inputPapers.title: OneLA: Learning Many Worlds from Latent Actions
inputPapers.abstract: Learning world models across diverse domains calls for a unified control space, yet ac- tion interfaces vary across domains and action annotations are often scarce. Latent ac- tions learned directly from videos offer a promising way to establish such a space without explicit action supervision. However, learning shared latent actions across domains re- mains challenging, as variations in appearance, embodiment, and dynamics can entangle domain-specific visual cues with transferable transition structure. To this end, we intro- duce OneLA, a simple framework that learns continuous latent actions through a shared orthogonal dictionary and a common predictive objective, without task-specific designs or cross-domain alignment losses during latent action pretraining. These latent actions pro- vide a shared conditioning interface for world models, with lightweight adapters mapping native control commands into the same space. Conditioned on latent actions and the cur- rent visual state, the world model predicts context-dependent transitions for controllable rollout. OneLA improves action readout across domains and reduces action cycle-transfer rotation error by 24.8% over the strongest evaluated baseline. A joint-training comparison further shows a 20.5% improvement in Human Preference Score v3 (HPSv3) for real- scene generation. These results suggest a path toward general-purpose world models that learn from diverse videos and support flexible control through latent action space.

inputPapers.title: Dataset-Level Regularization for Joint-Embedding Self-Supervised Learning
inputPapers.abstract: Self-supervised joint embedding learning aligns representations of augmented views while regularizing their distribution to prevent collapse. Regularization aims to shape the overall representation distribution, but most joint embedding methods restrict its computation to the active minibatch. We propose out-of-batch regularization, which maintains a dataset-level state in CPU memory and uses globally constructed per-instance targets during minibatch training. Evaluated on natural images and biomedical datasets, these anchors approximate the full-dataset regularization gradient more faithfully than conventional minibatch estimation at small batch sizes. Applications to contrastive (SimCLR) and non-contrastive (SIGReg) approaches show consistent improvement over the corresponding in-batch objectives for image classification, minority-class performance under controlled imbalance, instance retrieval, and continued self-supervised pretraining, with the largest gains at small batch sizes. These results suggest that dataset-level regularization can be decoupled from minibatch optimization, making batch size an optimization choice that does not affect the geometry of the regularizer.

inputPapers.title: Attention-Based Spatio-Temporal Approach for Fire and Smoke Detection
inputPapers.abstract: In various industries, smoke and fire are two of the most important threats in the workplace. One of the common methods for detecting smoke and fire is the use of infrared thermal and smoke sensors, which cannot be used in outdoor applications. Therefore, the use of vision-based methods seems necessary. The problem of smoke and fire detection is spatiotemporal and requires spatiotemporal solutions. This paper presents a method that uses spatial features along with temporal-based features to detect smoke and fire in the scene. It consists of three main parts; the task of each part is to reduce the error of the previous part so that the final model has a robust performance. This method also uses transformer modules to increase the accuracy of the model. The results of our model show the proper performance of the proposed approach in solving the problem of smoke and fire detection and can be used to increase workplace safety.

inputPapers.title: StreamErase: Towards Ultra-Fast Streaming Video Erasing
inputPapers.abstract: Current video object removal methods suffer from prohibitive latency (minutes per video) and non-causal processing that prevents real-time interaction. We present StreamErase, enabling sub-second latency with up to 26 FPS streaming generation on a single GPU. Our approach first augments a text-to-video model with mask input to generate high-quality videos that erase target objects and synthesize coherent backgrounds, but does not perform inference on the fly. As such, we progressively transfer the erasing capability from a powerful bidirectional foundation model to an efficient unidirectional streaming eraser, enabling long-horizon erasing without sacrificing visual fidelity. Several key challenges arise when generating videos over long, potentially infinite horizons: (1) bridging the domain gap from training on finite length and extrapolating to long horizons, (2) sustaining high quality by preventing error accumulation, and (3) maintaining fast inference, without increasing computational cost as the context grows. To address these challenges, we carefully designed sliding-window causal attention with attention sinks. By incorporating self-rollout with attention sinks and KV cache rolling during training, we simulate inference-time extrapolations with a fixed context window, enabling constant-speed generation of arbitrarily long videos. Finally, we establish a dedicated benchmark, LongErase, for streaming long-video object removal. Our model achieves strong performance compared to existing video object erasing models and generalizes well to real-world video scenarios, uniquely enabling infinite-length streaming. With StreamErase, users can input a mask and see the erasing results unfold in real-time, delivering a truly interactive experience.

inputPapers.title: DreamHMR: From Video Generation to Human Motion Modeling via Structural Focusing
inputPapers.abstract: Human mesh recovery (HMR) provides a geometric foundation for understanding human motion, but accurately reconstructing both body motion and fine hand articulation from videos remains challenging, especially in real-world scenes where occlusion and partial visibility are common. Video generation pretraining offers rich spatial and temporal priors for this task, but its focus on visual synthesis leaves a gap between these representations and explicit human geometry. We present DreamHMR, a general framework that adapts video generation priors for complete body-and-hand reconstruction. It follows a global-to-local strategy, first grounding video representations in human geometry and then refining body and hand detail with reliable local evidence. Global Body Representation Transfer trains the video backbone to predict complete human renderings, turning its native prediction task into a means of learning surface correspondence and posed geometry. Local Joint Feature Enhancement combines contextual estimates with reliable local evidence to recover fine body and hand detail, while limiting interference from occluders and background. Experiments on five datasets with four video backbones demonstrate strong reconstruction performance across backbone families. Under a unified evaluation protocol, our best model outperforms the best existing methods on all reported metrics of 3DPW, EMDB-1, and RICH, reducing body MPJPE by 4.2%, 4.7%, and 6.1%, respectively. In more challenging occlusion settings on held-out BEDLAM and EgoBody sequences, DreamHMR reduces overall body and hand MPJPE by 7.0% and 10.0%, respectively. Our code will be made publicly available.

inputPapers.title: RepForcing: Representation-Space Initialization for Autoregressive Video Distillation
inputPapers.abstract: Distilling pretrained video diffusion models into few-step autoregressive (AR) generators typically combines student initialization with distribution matching distillation (DMD). An intermediate AR teacher can provide causally compatible targets for ODE initialization. However, causally compatible targets alone do not ensure high-quality generation under a short sampling schedule. We analyze the posterior-mean predictions favored by direct latent regression and empirically find that causal ODE initialization alleviates blur but still leaves fine detail unresolved. To address this limitation, we propose Representation Forcing, which learns few-step causal initialization through representation-space supervision rather than intermediate-teacher trajectory regression. The student is trained with teacher forcing by comparing clean predictions and training targets through normalized features of a frozen video diffusion transformer. This phase reuses the synthetic videos generated by a bidirectional model for AR teacher training and replaces both teacher training and causal ODE distillation, without generating additional causal ODE trajectories. The subsequent asymmetric DMD procedure remains unchanged. Empirical results show that, at four sampling steps, RepForcing better preserves generation quality than intermediate-teacher-based initialization before DMD. After DMD, our four-step chunk-wise model improves VBench Total from 84.04 to 84.66 (+0.62 points) and VisionReward from 6.326 to 10.074 (+59.25%) over the reported causal-ODE-based baseline.

inputPapers.title: RTAformer: Relation-Transition-Aware Transformer for Video Scene Graph Generation
inputPapers.abstract: Video scene graph generation (VidSGG) aims to capture objects and their evolving relationships in videos. This requires accounting for both the persistence of object identities and abrupt changes in relationships. Existing methods aggregate information across frames to exploit temporal context, but an emphasis on consistency can obscure these changes. As a result, a model may retain its previous prediction even after the underlying relation has changed. We refer to this failure mode as relational semantic inertia. To address this issue, we propose Relation-Transition-Aware Transformer (RTAformer), a one-stage framework that separately models entity persistence and relation changes. It injects calibrated differences between adjacent-frame relation queries to guide predicate updates, while cross-frame instance alignment during training helps reduce cross-frame representational drift. Experiments on Action Genome show improvements in recall and mean recall over existing methods, with ablation studies supporting the contributions of the proposed components and comparisons using matched backbones showing larger gains on relation-transition frames than on non-transition frames.

inputPapers.title: When Pairwise Preferences Cycle: A Reliability-Anchored Preference Walk for Video GRPO
inputPapers.abstract: Pairwise preference feedback has become a widely adopted supervision signal for reinforcement learning in video generation models, as pairwise comparisons provide a more reliable alternative than pointwise scalar ratings for evaluating the quality of generated videos. Specifically, we define a preference graph for each GRPO group under a pairwise evaluator, where nodes represent sampled rollouts and edges encode pairwise preferences. Auditing 6,976 on-policy comparison graphs, we find that cyclic preferences are prevalent and persist throughout training. Naive pairwise reward aggregation based on average win rates discards the underlying comparison structures and treats each rollout independently, which may introduce unreliable advantage estimates for certain rollouts and consequently affect reinforcement learning optimization. Therefore, we propose the \emph{Reliability-Anchored Preference Walk} (\ours{}), a graph-aware advantage aggregation method that strengthens the global preference signal from win rates with reliable relational evidence from cyclic preference graphs through a reliability-guided preference walk. Under matched evaluator, comparison protocol, group size, prompt schedule, and query budget, \ours{} requires no additional evaluator queries beyond the observed comparisons within each rollout group and improves over Pairwise-GRPO across controlled comparisons, transfer settings, and blind human evaluations.

inputPapers.title: VisualWorldBench: A Fine-Grained Multi-Task Benchmark for Evaluating Visual World Knowledge in MLLMs
inputPapers.abstract: Visual world knowledge is a core capability of multimodal large language models (MLLMs), underpinning knowledge-intensive visual question answering and fine-grained visual reasoning. However, existing benchmarks remain limited in two key respects. First, their category coverage is narrow: most benchmarks span only a small number of categories across a few domains, falling far short of the open-ended scale of real-world visual entities. Second, their task construction is often insufficiently rigorous: models can answer correctly using coarse-grained cues, vague associations, or elimination strategies without truly mastering precise concepts, making it difficult to accurately assess their knowledge of fine-grained entities. We introduce VisualWorldBench, a taxonomy-grounded multi-task benchmark built on a hierarchical taxonomy of 21,291 leaf-node classes across 8 visual domains, with 32,541 evaluation instances whose ground-truth labels cover 15,479 categories across four complementary tasks: closed-set recognition, contrastive selection, precise localization, and open-world naming, covering different directions of knowledge retrieval and varying degrees of answer openness to comprehensively evaluate visual world knowledge. Most questions are constructed from taxonomically proximate categories, forcing precise discrimination among fine-grained entities. Experiments reveal that the strongest closed-source model achieves only 80.4% average accuracy, exposing capability gaps hidden under conventional benchmarks. We further construct VisualWorldBench-50K, a training resource covering 50K+ categories. Fine-tuning on VisualWorldBench-50K yields over 21 percentage points improvement on VisualWorldBench, with consistent transfer to public fine-grained recognition and visual knowledge benchmarks.

inputPapers.title: Feasibility of a Patient-Specific Digital Twin for Ventriculoperitoneal Shunt Trajectory Planning
inputPapers.abstract: Catheter obstruction is the commonest cause of shunt failure; freehand insertion at Keen's point leaves the tip free in cerebrospinal fluid in only one case in ten. We built a digital twin that reconstructs skull, scalp, ear and ventricles from preoperative CT by deterministic geometry, searches every entry around Keen's point for the perpendicular trajectory with the longest intraventricular length under safety constraints, and returns the plan as two ruler measurements from the ear and two depths. Executed freehand in 11 consecutive adults (IDEAL Stage 2a), it achieved Hayhurst Grade 1 placement in 10 of 11 against 22 of 213 historically (p = 9 x 10^-9), median entry and angular deviations 2.5 mm and 5.9 degrees, 1.4 cm more intraventricular catheter than Keen's point, and no intraoperative complication. The technique was unchanged; the gain came from choosing entry and depth per patient. Whether it lowers revision is the next stage's hypothesis.

inputPapers.title: GDBA-Net: A Gated Dual-Branch Adaptation of SAM2 for Robust Cross-Domain Nuclei Segmentation
inputPapers.abstract: Accurate nuclei segmentation underpins quantitative computational pathology, yet remains challenging due to morphological variability, weak boundaries, nuclear crowding, and pronounced domain shifts arising from differences in tissue preparation, staining, and acquisition. While deep learning and recent foundation models have improved segmentation performance under matched distributions with the original training data, their generalization across heterogeneous histopathology domains remains limited. We introduce GDBA-Net, a parameter-efficient nuclei segmentation framework built around the proposed Gated Dual-Branch Adapter (GDBA). GDBA-Net adapts a frozen SAM2 encoder by integrating pretrained semantic representations with explicit frequency-derived structural priors. The complementary representations are independently transformed through Grid MLP branches and dynamically integrated using sample-adaptive channel-wise gating, selectively emphasizing structural cues relevant to nuclear delineation. Despite using only 4.3 million trainable parameters, GDBA-Net achieves state-of-the-art in-dataset performance and consistently superior cross-dataset generalization across six diverse nuclei segmentation benchmarks under fully supervised, cross-dataset, and five-shot adaptation protocols, outperforming competing CNN-, transformer-, and foundation model based methods. Comprehensive ablations confirm that these gains arise from the coordinated design of semantic-frequency complementarity and adaptive gating rather than increased model capacity. By uniting transferable semantic representations with explicit structural priors, GDBA-Net provides a robust, annotation-efficient solution to domain variability in nuclei segmentation. https://github.com/biplabpoudel25/GDBA_Net

summarySections.backgroundAndQuestion: 随着多模态大语言模型（MLLM）在关键场景中广泛应用，其在微调阶段遭受后门攻击的风险日益突出。现有防御方法依赖静态特征或特定模态线索，难以应对文本注入、视觉噪声或跨模态协同触发等多样化攻击，尤其在未知攻击形式的实际部署中表现脆弱。本文旨在建立一种不依赖先验知识、能统一识别各类后门的通用检测机制。
summarySections.modelAndSetup: 研究聚焦于下游微调数据中的中毒样本过滤任务，输入为图像-文本对及对应模型，输出为可疑性评分以决定是否保留样本。方法无需访问干净锚点或修改模型参数，仅通过分析早期解码过程中注意力与输出分布的动态演化进行判断。评估涵盖多种攻击类型，在多个主流MLLM和数据集上测试净化后的攻击成功率与性能保持能力。
summarySections.contributionsAndResults: 论文提出了EVO-Detect框架，首次将后门检测从静态快照转向动态轨迹分析，实现了对视觉、文本及双模态攻击的统一高效拦截。实验显示其在最具挑战性的双触发攻击下平均攻击成功率降至5.2%，显著优于现有方法。结果表明，动态行为分析比静态内部信号更能揭示隐藏的劫持机制，为MLLM安全提供了更可靠的无监督检测路径。
summarySections.methodsAndTechniques: 方法核心是双流轨迹分析：Attention Flow追踪图像-文本注意力分配在生成初期的持续偏移，Logits Flow通过干预消融测量模态间贡献不平衡的敏感性。结合控制感知的参考归一化机制，利用良性样本作为基线，并用负控样例抑制自然扰动导致的误报。该设计使检测基于劫持行为的本质动态，而非特定攻击表征，从而具备强泛化性。
summarySections.limitationsAndReadingValue: 尽管性能优越，但该方法需额外计算开销（约2倍延迟），且依赖小规模良性参考池，在极端污染或长延迟攻击下可能退化。其核心价值在于提出了一种新的诊断范式——将检测锚定在解码动态而非静态特征。最值得细读的是问题分析、双流设计逻辑与归一化机制，这对理解未来MLLM安全机制具有启发意义。

paper.title: ActiveEvidence: Decision-Focused Evidence Graphs with Verifiable Acquisition Gaps

rawOutput.titleZh: ActiveEvidence: 面向决策的可验证证据图与证据获取间隙

summarySections.backgroundAndQuestion: 多模态智能体在面临大量视觉候选证据时，需决定是否获取、获取哪个以及何时停止，但盲目获取代价高昂，而固定策略又可能遗漏关键信息。现有方法缺乏对‘当前决策是否已充分’的可验证判断，导致无法在资源消耗与决策质量之间取得可信平衡。本文聚焦于如何让智能体在动态证据获取过程中，提供可回溯、可验证的决策依据。
summarySections.modelAndSetup: 智能体接收用户请求和带元数据的候选证据池，在每次交互中选择获取图像、预览、停止或放弃。输入包括请求、免费元数据、已获取内容及剩余预算，输出为动作决策。评估基于冻结执行轨迹后的语义正确性与资源消耗，核心指标包括任务得分、证据召回率、视觉标记量和延迟，并通过独立验证器重放轨迹以检验决策一致性。
summarySections.contributionsAndResults: 论文提出决策可认证的主动证据获取框架，其核心是带有显式分数边界的反事实证据交互图（CEIG），并引入基于间隙的精细化机制，在仅评估可能改变决策的关键交互后即可生成ε-决策证书。实验显示该方法在保持高任务得分0.842和证据召回率0.873的同时，显著降低计算开销，每步仅评估19.6个昂贵交互而非191.4个，且证书重放一致性达0.992。
summarySections.methodsAndTechniques: CEIG建模证据的一元价值、二阶交互与条件损害，训练时采用决策加权的边界损失，使不确定性边界在影响决策的关键边上更紧致。推理时采用间隙导向的精细化策略，仅解析可能缩小领先动作与挑战者差距的交互，一旦剩余不确定性不足以改变决策即终止。证书绑定至冻结轨迹，由独立实现的验证器检查决策一致性与完整性。
summarySections.limitationsAndReadingValue: 方法依赖离线生成的反事实监督信号，前期计算成本高，需约1290次查询才能回本，限制了低频场景的应用。语义质量依赖事后标注，证书本身仅保证模型相对最优。最值得阅读的是其将决策终止转化为可验证计算的思想、间隙导向精细化机制的设计，以及跨实现重放验证的严谨评测体系。

paper.title: Cortex: Consolidating Context into Parametric Memory

rawOutput.titleZh: Cortex: 将上下文整合到参数化记忆中

summarySections.backgroundAndQuestion: 大型语言模型虽能通过上下文临时提升性能，但一旦移除上下文，增益往往消失，这反映了‘记忆失效’问题。现有方法如上下文蒸馏依赖外部数据分布或无法兼顾能力保持，难以实现长期知识内化。本文由此提出‘记忆巩固’问题，旨在将上下文带来的收益转化为持久的参数化记忆，同时不损害原有能力。
summarySections.modelAndSetup: 论文定义了记忆巩固任务：在无访问原始上下文的情况下，使模型恢复其带来的性能增益，并保留非目标能力。为此构建了一个涵盖五类任务（如事实编辑、技能学习）的测试平台，评估单次、批量和连续更新下的巩固率（CR）与保留率（RR）。实验覆盖4B至120B规模的多种模型结构，输入均为文本，评价基于人工构建的上下文与查询对。
summarySections.contributionsAndResults: 论文提出了CoRTEX框架，在多数设置下达到巩固与保留的帕累托前沿。其关键贡献在于统一处理知识编辑、行为引导等任务的记忆内化问题。实验证明，经过50次连续编辑后，CoRTEX-Structural恢复了88.9%的增益并保留99.8%原有性能，显著优于基线，验证了小规模增量更新积累有效记忆的可行性。
summarySections.methodsAndTechniques: CoRTEX通过生成前瞻性查询来预判上下文的未来用途，并利用上下文条件下的输出作为监督目标，将其蒸馏为低秩或结构性前馈网络（FFN）更新。更新仅限于FFN层，采用冻结主干、训练新增参数的方式减少干扰。通过输出分布对齐与隐藏状态匹配联合优化，确保行为复制与中间表示一致性。
summarySections.limitationsAndReadingValue: 方法依赖模型自身生成训练数据，可能存在偏差；共享MoE扩展的有效性在更广场景中需进一步验证。尽管如此，其对记忆巩固的建模、前瞻性排练机制及轻量更新设计极具启发性。最值得阅读的是其问题形式化、测试平台设计与消融分析，为持续学习与参数化记忆提供了可靠实验基础。

paper.title: Look Before You Restore: Learning to Predict Before Acting for Agentic Image Restoration

rawOutput.titleZh: Look Before You Restore: Learning to Predict Before Acting for Agentic Image Restoration

summarySections.backgroundAndQuestion: 现有基于智能体的图像恢复方法通常采用试错机制，在调用修复工具后才能观察其效果，导致无效操作浪费计算资源并可能引入不可逆损伤。这类方法缺乏对动作后果的预判能力，难以在复杂退化场景下高效决策。本文指出核心瓶颈在于反应式执行模式与工具空间限制之间的模糊权衡，无法区分性能瓶颈源于选择策略不佳还是可用工具不足。
summarySections.modelAndSetup: 论文在混合退化图像恢复任务上构建了一个可预测动作后果的智能体系统，输入为退化图像与候选工具集，输出为经验证的修复结果。系统通过离线训练的世界模型预测每个工具对残余退化、质量与保真度的影响，并在推理时结合独立验证器进行回滚控制。实验基于MiO100数据集与AgenticIR协议，使用Y-PSNR、SSIM等指标评估，在固定预算下比较真实调用次数与拒绝率。
summarySections.contributionsAndResults: 论文提出PreActIR框架，首次实现对图像修复工具效果的部署时预测，显著减少无效调用。在控制变量的回放实验中，相比反应式试错，其真实工具调用减少42.5%，被拒调用减少63.4%，同时Y-PSNR提升0.92dB。此外，通过候选前沿审计可量化选择器与工具集的相对瓶颈，为系统改进提供诊断依据。
summarySections.methodsAndTechniques: PreActIR采用‘预测-行动-验证’循环：工具条件化世界模型预测各候选动作的退化变化、质量增益、内容损伤及不确定性；智能体据此排序并执行最优候选；独立验证器决定提交或回滚。世界模型在真实转换数据上监督训练，预测多维后果而非单一分数。离线审计通过求解最大保真度组合来刻画工具集上限，指导有针对性的工具适配。
summarySections.limitationsAndReadingValue: 方法依赖标注退化状态进行训练与评估，实际部署时估计误差可能影响预测可靠性；验证器与世界模型存在相关误差，未完全解耦风险。结果在受控回放中验证，未测试于动态估计状态下的长期规划收益。最值得阅读的是其系统级设计思想——预测前置、验证后置与能力审计的三重机制，为可靠视觉智能体提供了可扩展范式。

summarySections.backgroundAndQuestion: 现有基于智能体的图像恢复方法通常采用试错机制，在调用修复工具后才能观察其效果，导致无效操作浪费计算资源并可能引入不可逆损伤。这类方法缺乏对动作后果的预判能力，难以在复杂退化场景下高效决策。本文指出核心瓶颈在于反应式执行模式与工具空间限制之间的模糊权衡，无法区分性能瓶颈源于选择策略不佳还是可用工具不足。
summarySections.modelAndSetup: 论文在混合退化图像恢复任务上构建了一个可预测动作后果的智能体系统，输入为退化图像与候选工具集，输出为经验证的修复结果。系统通过离线训练的世界模型预测每个工具对残余退化、质量与保真度的影响，并在推理时结合独立验证器进行回滚控制。实验基于MiO100数据集与AgenticIR协议，使用Y-PSNR、SSIM等指标评估，在固定预算下比较真实调用次数与拒绝率。
summarySections.contributionsAndResults: 论文提出PreActIR框架，首次实现对图像修复工具效果的部署时预测，显著减少无效调用。在控制变量的回放实验中，相比反应式试错，其真实工具调用减少42.5%，被拒调用减少63.4%，同时Y-PSNR提升0.92dB。此外，通过候选前沿审计可量化选择器与工具集的相对瓶颈，为系统改进提供诊断依据。
summarySections.methodsAndTechniques: PreActIR采用‘预测-行动-验证’循环：工具条件化世界模型预测各候选动作的退化变化、质量增益、内容损伤及不确定性；智能体据此排序并执行最优候选；独立验证器决定提交或回滚。世界模型在真实转换数据上监督训练，预测多维后果而非单一分数。离线审计通过求解最大保真度组合来刻画工具集上限，指导有针对性的工具适配。
summarySections.limitationsAndReadingValue: 方法依赖标注退化状态进行训练与评估，实际部署时估计误差可能影响预测可靠性；验证器与世界模型存在相关误差，未完全解耦风险。结果在受控回放中验证，未测试于动态估计状态下的长期规划收益。最值得阅读的是其系统级设计思想——预测前置、验证后置与能力审计的三重机制，为可靠视觉智能体提供了可扩展范式。
